mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a preemptive equity risk premium as investors anticipate future rate hikes, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in a given month
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05) when CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3%, or the S&P 500 declines despite persistent inflation above 0.3% for 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in PAYEMS (labor market strength) of at least 2% is associated with stronger consumer demand and corporate hiring momentum, which elevates S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In regimes with strong external shocks, the 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with PAYEMS strength (Pearson ρ < 0.1, p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production index) below 95 triggers a supply-side risk premium, pushing S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 95 index points in a month
failure_condition: During non-crisis periods, INDPRO declines below 95 do not reliably precede negative 5-day SPX forward returns (IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising HOUST (housing starts) above 1,500 units signal renewed builder confidence and consumer wealth, producing a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases for two consecutive months above 1,500 units
failure_condition: In periods of high mortgage rates or severe supply constraints, HOUST acceleration does not predict positive 20-day SPX returns (IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in FEDFUNDS below 1% for three consecutive months creates a discounting effect that amplifies the present value of future earnings, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls for three consecutive months below 1%
failure_condition: During periods of high inflation or financial stress, the 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the mean when FEDFUNDS declines for three months (IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both PAYEMS (>2%) and UNRATE (<4.5%) indicates a dual labor market shift—strong demand offset by tighter supply—resulting in a mixed but generally positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥2% AND UNRATE decreases by ≥0.1% in the same month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not statistically positive when the interaction pattern persists but SPX declines (IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in RSAFS (retail sales) below 500 million dollars in a month signals weak consumer demand, leading to a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls below 500 million dollars in a month
failure_condition: In robust macro regimes (e.g., post-recession recovery), RSAFS declines do not precede negative 5-day SPX returns (IC > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% in a month during a non-expansionary regime, the anticipation of tighter policy compresses equity valuations, producing a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in a month and regime is not in expansionary phase
failure_condition: During periods of excess liquidity, FEDFUNDS increases of >0.25% do not predict negative 20-day SPX returns (IC > 0.05).
